question: On the two still-unconsumed CrowdBot decision sessions, does the existing production detector-conditioned temporal geometry contribution improve accepted production-pipeline replay alert-decision timing or scored event discrimination relative to the otherwise identical production chain with that contribution neutralized?

estimand.within_session_dependence: The scored events and windows are observational paired items nested in two distinct capture sessions from one CrowdBot source, day and collection context. Neither the items nor the two sessions are claimed to be independent population samples. No population p-value or confidence interval is authorized.
estimand.paired_contrast: branch B minus branch A under one shared per-frame detector output ledger

endpoint_estimands.EARLY_RESPONSE: Among the frozen scoreable positive events with an accepted valid replay alert in both branches, the paired first-alert decision-frame lead of B versus A.
endpoint_estimands.RISK_DISCRIMINATION: On the fixed 15 scored positive-event or negative-window items, the paired difference in item correctness between B and A.

rationale.lite_r2: BOTH_NOT_READY_FOR_CONFIRMATION / IMPLEMENTATION_NOT_READY; not rerun or connected to Android
rationale.production_observation: TemporalRiskTracker already computes target-conditioned causal temporal geometry from at most five detection observations over 900 ms and can affect the existing unified risk, lifecycle and feedback chain.
rationale.selection_reason: Factorizing an already deployed code path answers the end-to-end dual-loop question with less implementation distance and greater product relevance than routing first through D0, EVIMO2v2 and JRDB.
rationale.novelty_limit: The second loop is detector-conditioned temporal box geometry, not an independent sensor or object-agnostic geometry source.

non_goals: rewrite or rescue Sparse LK F-1B
inspect candidate output before the contract and implementation lock are frozen
select tracker thresholds, windows, labels, regions or endpoint rules after output access
add depth, optical flow, segmentation, ARCore or a new fusion policy
change the default production model, alert policy, cooldown, fatigue or feedback semantics
claim Confirmation, generalization, product benefit or safety

truth_ledger.historical_nonconsumption_field: Both DECISION session rows declare candidate_outputs_executed=false. This is a bound historical record, while the new R0 namespace absence is machine-verified by both preflight receipts.

precomputed_scored_frame_support.handling: Retain and report all 17 frozen truth items. Mark F1A-P-007 and F1A-P-009 TEMPORAL_SCORING_NOT_EVALUABLE before candidate execution because their conservative valid-alert intervals map to zero frozen frames. Do not count them as branch misses, do not include them in either endpoint denominator, and do not widen their truth intervals.

frozen_data.source_clock: source_capture_timestamp_ns from each frozen frame ledger
frozen_data.session_processing: Process every frozen RGB frame in strictly increasing source timestamp order; reset both branches only at the session boundary; preserve native frame gaps.
frozen_data.unscored_gaps: Frames outside frozen positive events and negative windows remain in state history and the trace but do not become implicit negative truth.
forbidden_inputs: old F-1B Sparse LK or A/B candidate output
LITE R0 or R1 failed output
LITE R2 output as an input to this candidate

detector_contract.qnn_route_parity: Use the production provider's HTP backend, FP16 precision, sustained-high-performance mode, native-library directory and CPU thread settings. The formal runner is strict and must fail before start instead of taking the production provider's CPU fallback.
detector_contract.single_inference_rule: Run the detector exactly once per frame and feed the exact same immutable detection list to A and B.
detector_contract.failure_rule: Any decoder, detector initialization, inference, postprocess or frame-order exception invalidates the formal execution; a valid empty detection list is not a failure.

input_identity_receipt.generator_identity: Bound inside the receipt hashed above.

truth_membership_receipt.generator_identity: Bound inside the receipt hashed above.

decision_policy.gateway_semantics: Each branch owns an independent production FeedbackController, including its direction/proximity cooldown and FeedbackFatigueController state. Its clock is the shared source nowMs for the current frame. Frozen speech and haptic ports are always ready and return accepted=true; no Android TTS or vibrator service is invoked.
decision_policy.claim_wording: A valid accepted replay alert means the production control path accepted at least one frozen always-ready output port. It is not proof that a physical effect was emitted, perceived or useful to a person.
decision_policy.risk_event_scope: The default RiskEventTracker does not track object-detector persons. It remains present and identical in both branches, but same-event suppression must not be credited as an evaluated behavior on these CrowdBot object-detector inputs.
decision_policy.session_reset: Reset each AssistDecisionKernel and its own FeedbackController once immediately before each session; never reset within a session.

branch_a.temporal_history: updated from the same detections and timestamps
branch_a.allowed_external_effect: For DetectionSource.OBJECT_DETECTOR only, return the unmodified per-frame RiskAnalyzer output with ApproachTrend.UNKNOWN after updating the same tracker history; no object-detector temporal motion promotion, temporal message change or temporal score contribution is externally applied. DetectionSource.SEGMENTATION and external risk-evidence behavior remain on the current production rules.
branch_a.downstream: current RiskStabilizer, RiskEventTracker, side-person confirmation, FeedbackController including cooldown/fatigue, FeedbackPlanner and effect receipt

branch_b.temporal_tracker: current default TemporalRiskTracker, max five frames and 900 ms

factorization.only_permitted_difference: Whether object-detector-conditioned TemporalRiskTracker output is externally applied before otherwise identical per-branch stabilizer/event/feedback chains.
factorization.state_isolation: A and B own separate AssistDecisionKernel, AssistEngine, TemporalRiskTracker, RiskStabilizer, RiskEventTracker, side-person confirmation, FeedbackController, fatigue state and SessionTrace instances. The only shared runtime value is an immutable canonical copy of the single per-frame DetectorFrameResult and the same source timestamps.
factorization.production_parity_guard: With the default mode enabled, all existing focused TemporalRiskTracker, AssistEngine, AssistDecisionKernel and scene-replay tests must remain byte-for-byte or field-for-field equivalent. Mutation tests must prove that the neutralized mode removes object-detector temporal effects while retaining the same pre-temporal semantic result and downstream chain. A segmentation fixture must prove stable-segmentation promotion is identical in A and B.
factorization.order_invariance_guard: Synthetic mutation replay must produce identical per-branch results when branch invocation order is A-then-B versus B-then-A.
factorization.implementation_lock_requirement: Before activation, bind every modified source, the device producer, producer validator, evaluator, accepting-port implementation, Gradle/QNN dependency identity, test APK SHA-256, ABI and all transitively used feedback-policy identities.
forbidden_difference: different risk thresholds, labels, regions or target matching
different stabilizer, event, confirmation, feedback or cooldown configuration
new depth, flow, segmentation or route evidence
sharing mutable kernel, gateway, event, stabilizer or trace state between branches

producer_input_allowlist: the RGB files referenced by those ledgers
forbidden_producer_inputs: any truth, adjudication or expected-alert file
producer_firewall.pilot_rule: Pilot and mutation work may use synthetic fixtures only. No decision RGB frame may be decoded before implementation review and formal activation.
publication_order: producer writes an atomic truth-blind trace and producer receipt
independent validator verifies code/input/backend identities, detector_invocation_count=4422, row_count=8844, pair hashes, failures and truth_joined=false
validated trace and receipt are hashed and sealed
only then may a separate evaluator process open the frozen truth ledger
producer_firewall.operator_visibility: Do not inspect, summarize or render candidate trace content before the independent producer validator passes and the sealed trace hash is recorded.

trace_contract.detector_output_binding: Invoke the detector exactly 4422 times. The A and B row for every frame must carry the same canonical detector_output_sha256 and pre_temporal_raw_risk_sha256; canonicalize the immutable detection list before the first branch call and verify the hash is unchanged after both branch calls.
trace_contract.source_time_binding: Pass the same source-derived nowMs and decisionAtNs to both branches. Invoke AssistDecisionKernel directly; do not route formal replay through AssistSessionCoordinator, FpsTracker or a wall-clock scheduler.
trace_contract.publication: Write the truth-blind branch trace atomically and hash it before opening the event ledger for evaluation.
trace_contract.progress: Expose session, completed frames, total 4422 frames, throughput, ETA and terminal state.
trace_contract.full_denominator: All 4422 frames and both branch rows remain present; failures are rows and invalidate rather than disappearing.

truth_join.positive_valid_alert_window: Convert seconds to integer nanoseconds by exact decimal multiplication by 1,000,000,000; use the closed interval from alertable_start_interval_seconds.end through end_or_clear_interval_seconds.start. This conservative interior excludes label-uncertainty margins.
truth_join.positive_premature_window: After the same exact decimal-to-integer-nanosecond conversion, use the half-open interval from onset_interval_seconds.start inclusive through alertable_start_interval_seconds.start exclusive.
truth_join.negative_window: After exact decimal multiplication by 1,000,000,000, use the complete closed frozen window_interval_seconds interval.
truth_join.valid_deliverable_alert: feedback_triggered=true inside the positive valid-alert window under the production FeedbackController with frozen accepting ports
truth_join.negative_false_alert: feedback_triggered=true inside a frozen negative window under the production FeedbackController with frozen accepting ports
truth_join.unscored_trigger: A trigger outside all frozen scored intervals is reported but cannot count as a false alert or a success.
truth_join.boundary_priority: A frame is assigned to at most one scored class. Valid-positive membership takes priority, then premature-positive, then negative. The bound truth-membership receipt proves zero cross-item or cross-class frame overlap under these rules.
truth_join.event_first_alert: Earliest valid deliverable alert per branch and positive event.
truth_join.timestamp_mapping: Subtract the first source_capture_timestamp_ns in the session and divide by 1e9; do not use inference completion or wall-clock time for event truth.

numeric_conventions.interval_membership: Use truth_join per class: valid-positive and negative intervals are closed [start,end]; premature-positive intervals are half-open [start,end).
numeric_conventions.median: Sort finite values ascending; for an odd count use the center value and for an even count use the arithmetic mean of the two center values.

session_frame_interval.rule: For each session, compute every strictly positive consecutive source_capture_timestamp_ns delta across the complete frozen frame ledger and take the median before converting nanoseconds to seconds.

numeric_conventions.gain_and_normalized_gain: Compute gain_ns as the exact integer source timestamp of A first alert minus B first alert. For each eligible event, normalized_gain_frames is the exact rational gain_ns divided by its session median delta-ns; compare the pooled median to 1.0 without first rounding individual ratios.
numeric_conventions.non_finite_rule: Any non-finite timestamp, gain, score or required numeric field invalidates execution.
numeric_conventions.comparison_tolerance: No epsilon or rounding is used for endpoint predicates; retain full parsed numeric precision and round only display copies.

common_guardrails: B positive-event recall, defined as the count of positive events with at least one valid deliverable alert, must not be below A.
B missed-positive-event count on the fixed 8-event scored positive denominator must not exceed A.
B false-alert-window count, defined as the count of negative windows with at least one false alert, must not exceed A.
B premature-alert-event count, defined as the count of positive events with at least one premature alert, must not exceed A.
B unscored-trigger frame count over the complete two-session trace must not exceed A.
There must be zero scored positive events where A has a valid alert and B misses, checked pooled and separately by session.
There must be zero negative windows where A is clean and B has a false alert, checked pooled and separately by session.
There must be zero scored positive events where A has no premature alert and B has a premature alert, checked pooled and separately by session.
Both sessions must be present with their complete fixed event/window denominators.
No gain may be created by decode, detector, branch, timing or output failure.

early_response.eligible_pairs: Positive events with a valid deliverable alert in both A and B.
early_response.gain_seconds: first_alert_time_A minus first_alert_time_B; positive means B is earlier.
success: Strictly more than half of eligible pairs have gain_seconds > 0.
For every eligible event, normalized_gain_frames follows numeric_conventions; the pooled median normalized_gain_frames is at least 1.0.
The median gain_seconds is greater than 0 in each of the two sessions.
At least two distinct positive events contribute positive gain.

risk_discrimination.positive_correct: At least one valid deliverable alert in the positive event.
risk_discrimination.negative_correct: Zero false alerts in the negative window.
risk_discrimination.paired_correctness_delta: Count(B correct and A incorrect) minus Count(A correct and B incorrect) on the fixed 15-item scored denominator: 8 frame-evaluable positives plus 7 negatives.
success: Each session contributes at least one B-correct/A-incorrect item.

risk_continuity.reason: R0 freezes neither continuous-risk truth nor a risk-gap endpoint for object-detector persons. No continuity proxy may be invented after output.

scientific_terminal.EARLY_RESPONSE: early_response success and risk_discrimination not success
scientific_terminal.RISK_DISCRIMINATION: risk_discrimination success and early_response evaluable but not success
scientific_terminal.RISK_DISCRIMINATION_WITH_EARLY_RESPONSE_: risk_discrimination success while early_response.evaluable is false
scientific_terminal.NO_INCREMENT: both endpoints are evaluable, neither succeeds, and execution is valid
scientific_terminal.EARLY_RESPONSE_NOT_EVALUABLE_RISK_DISCRI: early_response.evaluable is false, risk_discrimination is evaluable but does not succeed, and execution is valid
scientific_terminal.NOT_EVALUABLE_PRESTART: Before the formal-start marker, the frozen environment cannot initialize and live-probe the required backend or the fixed truth/input contract is unavailable. No decision RGB inference has begun.
scientific_terminal.INVALID_EXECUTION: Any failure after the formal-start marker, including before, during or after the first decision-frame inference; also any identity drift, missing frame/branch row, fallback backend, exception, non-atomic partial output, detector/pre-temporal mismatch between branches or forbidden input access.
scientific_terminal.formal_start: Write the formal-start marker atomically immediately before invoking detector inference for the first decision frame. Every failure before the marker is NOT_EVALUABLE_PRESTART; every failure after it is INVALID_EXECUTION.
scientific_terminal.one_shot: A formal-start marker consumes this evidence version. Do not rerun the same version after any valid, invalid or interrupted post-start attempt; a named repair requires a new protocol/output identity.
scientific_terminal.no_post_output_rescue: Do not change thresholds, windows, endpoints, labels, temporal mode or data after candidate output access.

multiplicity_and_reporting.endpoint_order: EARLY_RESPONSE and RISK_DISCRIMINATION are two co-decision endpoints in a pre-registered union directional screen. The terminal reports their joint truth table rather than selecting the better endpoint post hoc. Any positive terminal requires independent Confirmation.
multiplicity_and_reporting.inference: Descriptive fixed-sample directional screen only; do not calculate or report population p-values, independence-based confidence intervals or generalized effectiveness.
required_tables: all 17 truth items with session membership, including the two preflight temporal-scoring exclusions
all 8 scored positive first-alert times, eligibility and gain values
positive-event recall/miss, negative-window false-alert, premature-event and unscored-trigger-row totals separately from trigger-row counts
every common guardrail and terminal predicate as a machine-recomputed boolean

positive_terminal: Freeze an independent session/source Confirmation contract without using it for selection or tuning.
Retain branch B as the already-existing production behavior; add only factorized logging and verification needed to prove live CameraX/QNN parity.
Do not claim safety or real-user efficacy.
no_increment: Keep the production tracker as existing product logic but do not use this evidence for a paper dual-loop claim.
Repair D0 as operational canary routing with temporal-dependence sensitivity before any D0 implementation or execution.
conditional_successor.not_evaluable_or_invalid: Repair only the named environment, input or implementation fault in a new evidence version; do not reinterpret missing evidence as no increment.
